front.title: Effect Acknowledgement for HTTP and Web Linking

abstract.t: This document defines an Experimental HTTP binding for the QIK-VRT Effect Acknowledgement protocol. It introduces two Structured Fields and a Web Linking relation for capability discovery, preparation of a protected effect, validation of a full EFFECT_ACK responsibility record, and an exact-bound commit.

The binding is opt-in and does not redefine HTTP transport acknowledgement or method semantics. Generic HTTP and HTML implementations can ignore the extension. A client that elects fail-closed protection, however, does not send a protected effect until support has been discovered and an EFFECT_ACK_DONE record has been independently validated.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: HTTP success, transport acknowledgement, successful parsing and application return values do not establish authorization for an external effect. The EFFECT_ACK core protocol separates those concepts. This document maps that gate to HTTP without changing HTTP itself.

The binding uses Structured Field Values for HTTP and Web Linking . The same registered link relation can be represented in the HTTP Link field or by an HTML link element, providing one discovery model for protocol software and browsers.

section.name: Conventions and Requirements
section.t: The key words MUST, MUST NOT, REQUIRED, SHALL, SHALL NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, RECOMMENDED, NOT RECOMMENDED, MAY, and OPTIONAL are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.

This document assumes the five-state EFFECT_ACK core model: EFFECT_NACK, EFFECT_ACK_CONTINUE, EFFECT_ACK_DONE, EFFECT_ACK_ISOLATE and EFFECT_ACK_BLOCK. Only a fresh, authenticated, independently validated EFFECT_ACK_DONE record can be eligible for ordinary release.

section.name: Capability Discovery
section.t: An origin supporting this profile SHOULD advertise an effect-ack link relation. Discovery is metadata only and never authorizes an effect.
An HTML representation MAY advertise the same relation:
A fail-closed client MUST establish support before sending a protected operation in prepare mode. If support cannot be established, the client MUST NOT send the protected effect.

section.name: Effect-Ack-Request Field
section.t: Effect-Ack-Request is an HTTP request field whose value is a Structured Dictionary. Version 1 defines the following members:

tr.td: Protocol version; value 1 in this document.
Opaque single-use commit token. Required for commit and absent for prepare.
32-octet SHA-256 digest of the canonical responsibility record. Required for commit.

section.sourcecode: Effect-Ack-Request: v=1, mode=prepare Effect-Ack-Request: v=1, mode=commit, token=:AQIDBAUGBwgJCgsMDQ4PEA==:, hash=:AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=:
section.t: A server receiving prepare MUST NOT execute the protected effect. It MAY validate, simulate, preview, reserve or perform other work that deployment policy explicitly classifies as non-protected.

section.name: Effect-Ack Field
section.t: Effect-Ack is primarily an HTTP response field whose value is a Structured Dictionary. Version 1 defines:

tr.td: nack, continue, done, isolate or block.
32-octet SHA-256 digest of the full canonical responsibility record.
Opaque commit token, present only when commit can be attempted.

section.t: The compact field does not replace the full responsibility record. A consumer MUST obtain the exact record from the effect-ack link target or another authenticated channel and MUST independently validate it before commit.
section.sourcecode: Effect-Ack: v=1, state=done, hash=:AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=:, token=:AQIDBAUGBwgJCgsMDQ4PEA==: Link: </effect-ack/records/42>; rel="effect-ack"; type="application/json"

section.name: Prepare and Commit Transaction

ol.li: The client discovers the profile and decides that the proposed operation is protected.
The client transmits the exact proposed operation with mode=prepare. The server MUST NOT perform the protected effect.
The server evaluates the request under the EFFECT_ACK core protocol. A non-DONE result is returned without ordinary release.

For a DONE result the server MAY issue a single-use, short-lived token. The token MUST be integrity-protected and bound to the effective request target, method, request-content digest, policy digest, responsible principal, record hash and expiration.
The client obtains and independently validates the full responsibility record.
The client repeats the exact operation with mode=commit, the token and record hash.
The server atomically revalidates token freshness, single use, request equivalence, policy, record integrity and DONE state. Only then MAY the protected effect occur.
After execution, the deployment SHOULD expose a post-effect observation that can be bound into a successor record. A successful response alone is not post-effect proof.

section.t: Any difference in method, effective request target, content digest, policy binding, responsible principal, token freshness or record hash MUST prevent commit.

section.name: Backward Compatibility
section.t: The extension is opt-in. A generic HTTP recipient can ignore unknown fields according to HTTP semantics. Therefore, a fail-closed client MUST NOT send a protected operation to a server merely hoping that Effect-Ack-Request will be understood. Capability discovery or a deployment-configured equivalent is a prerequisite.

Servers MAY continue legacy behavior for endpoints that local policy does not classify as protected. A protected endpoint SHOULD reject an effect-bearing request that omits the required commit binding. This allows incremental deployment without redefining legacy HTTP.

section.name: HTML Integration
section.t: No new HTML element or parser behavior is defined. The registered Web Linking relation is expressed through the ordinary HTML link element. Browser software can discover the relation and expose a terminal, confirmation flow or other user interface without changing the document format.
The presence of an HTML link is discovery evidence only. It MUST NOT be interpreted as DONE.

section.name: Browser Proxy Considerations
section.t: A browser extension can implement this profile while remaining compatible with unmodified servers and pages. It can discover the link relation, keep protected requests in a local prepare state, validate a returned full record, and issue commit only after DONE.

Audio, video and screen capture remain Web-platform permission events. Media bytes are not EFFECT_ACK evidence until the user explicitly submits them. A browser proxy MUST NOT silently capture or transmit media and MUST preserve a visible distinction between local preview, submitted input, prepared effect and committed effect.

A proxy that renders other clients or backend states SHOULD normalize observations into a transport-neutral terminal frame while preserving source identifiers, exact record hashes, timestamps and uncertainty. Rendering is not authorization.

section.name: Intermediaries, Caches and CORS
section.t: Intermediaries MUST NOT synthesize an Effect-Ack field. A transformation that changes bound request semantics invalidates a prepare token unless the transformation itself is included in the binding.

An authorization result is not a reusable cache validator. A cached DONE assertion MUST NOT authorize a different request or later effect. Responsibility records containing sensitive metadata SHOULD use appropriate cache controls.

Script access to response fields remains subject to ordinary Fetch and CORS rules. An origin that intends cross-origin script access explicitly exposes the field. Privileged extensions operate under separately granted browser permissions and MUST NOT treat those permissions as effect authorization.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: Threats include forged DONE assertions, token theft, replay, request substitution between prepare and commit, downgrade, stale record reuse, policy substitution, alternate-path bypass, confused deputies and compromised evaluators. The full responsibility record and deployment authentication remain authoritative; the compact HTTP field is insufficient by itself.

Commit tokens MUST be unguessable, single-use, short-lived and exact-request bound. Consumers MUST rederive the EFFECT_ACK state. A browser or backend MUST NOT translate NACK, CONTINUE, ISOLATE or BLOCK into a releasing action.
HTTP Message Signatures MAY be used by a deployment profile to bind relevant HTTP components, but this specification does not require a particular signature system.

section.name: Privacy Considerations
section.t: Responsibility records can expose principals, policy identifiers and evidence references. Implementations SHOULD minimize metadata, avoid placing sensitive records in broadly cacheable responses, and retain media locally until explicit submission.

section.name: Example Exchange
section.sourcecode:
GET /.well-known/effect-ack HTTP/1.1 Host: example.test
HTTP/1.1 200 OK Link: </.well-known/effect-ack>; rel="effect-ack"; type="application/json"
POST /effect HTTP/1.1 Host: example.test Effect-Ack-Request: v=1, mode=prepare Content-Digest: sha-256=:...:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK Effect-Ack: v=1, state=done, hash=:...:, token=:...: Link: </effect-ack/records/42>; rel="effect-ack"; type="application/json"
POST /effect HTTP/1.1 Host: example.test Effect-Ack-Request: v=1, mode=commit, token=:...:, hash=:...: Content-Digest: sha-256=:...:
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content Effect-Ack: v=1, state=done, hash=:...:
